name: fs_large_multicluster_file_uefi
why: 64 MiB usb0 formats with 1 sector per cluster (pick_spc), so 512-byte clusters. Shell write caps content at 100 bytes, so Dolphin builds the file: 27 lines of 79 chars plus newlines = 2160 bytes, more than 4 clusters. Under UEFI the PIT is in poll mode, so ESC runs save_inner then close_clean. Covers multi-cluster write, read, cp into a subdirectory, reopen (27 lines), re-save without the trailing newline (2159 bytes), overwrite with a tiny file (frees the old chain), and delete. Typing 2160 chars through sendkey is slow (one editor redraw per key). (ESC opens the ':' prompt on UEFI too now that both paths have timer interrupts; 'x' saves and closes.)

name: fs_large_multicluster_file_grub
why: The same file of more than 4 clusters (2160 bytes) under GRUB. There the PIT is IRQ-driven, so ESC opens Dolphin's ':' prompt, which first waits for the ESC release scancode (0x81) from key_queue. That only arrives with real PS/2 input, which QEMU sendkey provides.

name: shell_history_left_right
why: LEFT and RIGHT browse an oldest-first history of up to 100 entries; consecutive duplicates are not added. RIGHT past the newest entry restores the draft, and an empty Enter runs nothing and is not recorded. A special-key step sends only that key; send '' presses Enter alone. Needs a fresh boot, so these are the only history entries.

why: autocomplete_command fills in only when exactly one available_commands entry starts with the typed prefix. Bare 'cat' also matches its own subcommands, so nothing completes. 'disk -ins' completes to 'disk -install' with no trailing space, which the -install parser rejects. Notation: 'abc<TAB>' means type abc, press TAB, then Enter.

name: shell_scrollback_keys
why: In the shell, UP and DOWN move the scrollback one line; PGUP and PGDN move 10 lines. Typing a printable key or Enter jumps back to the live view first, and DOWN or PGDN at the bottom do nothing. These keys print no text of their own, so the test checks for no fault and that the live prompt still runs commands afterwards.

name: empty_and_whitespace_lines
why: Empty lines must do nothing (execute_command returns when command[0]=='\0'). Whitespace-only lines are not empty and must print 'Command not found'. TAB on an empty buffer must not autocomplete anything. Backspace on an empty buffer must not underflow input_index (kmain checks input_index>0). The shell must still answer help afterwards.

name: unknown_commands_and_near_misses
why: Exact-match commands (strcmp) given extra arguments must be rejected. Prefix commands typed without their trailing space (rm, go and so on) must fall through to 'Command not found'. The legacy init_drive path must print its redirect text. 'stop now' must NOT power off, which shows the shutdown path is exact-match only. (Steps duplicated in shell_unknown_and_malformed_commands were dropped.)

name: max_length_127_and_overflow
why: kmain caps input_index at INPUT_MAX=127. A 200- or 306-char burst must be cut to exactly 127 chars, with no overflow of input_buffer[128] or the 128-byte history slot. The serial mirror drops soft wraps, so a run of 128 identical chars anywhere (echo or 'Command:' line) means the cap failed. The 128-char repeating line must lose its last char. 'uptime' must still parse cleanly afterwards because the buffer is memset after each command.

name: special_keys_backspace_and_autocomplete
why: Real PS/2 keys via sendkey: <LEFT> recalls history, PgUp/PgDn/Esc at the prompt print nothing and must not fault. Backspace bursts must not underflow. TAB autocomplete: a unique prefix completes (syscal -> syscalls, mon -ul -> mon -ultramon); an ambiguous prefix (d, wrap -o, cl -g matching -gettime and -getime) leaves the buffer unchanged. TAB on a 126-char buffer must not push input past 127. Repeated TAB on a complete command must not duplicate text.

name: history_overflow_104_entries
why: Alternating two commands gets past the duplicate-of-last filter. The resulting 104 entries exceed HISTORY_SIZE=100, so every command after the 100th takes the shift-down path in add_to_history (99 slots of 128 bytes copied each time). The 127-char entry tests the bounded copy into a 128-byte slot. History recall after overflow must return valid strings: no stale slot 0 and no read past history_count. The shell must stay responsive throughout.

name: bad_args_mem_cpu_cl_wrap_dev
why: Each option family must reject garbage, double spaces and trailing extras with its own 'Unknown <x> option' line. It must accept the undashed aliases (opt_is) and produce output for every valid option without faulting. wrap is turned off and back on.

name: bad_args_catalog_drive
why: catalog builds a string of about 6 KB in a fixed buffer, and every kind must fit. drive -cmd copies the name into tmp[128] with an explicit bound, then passes the rest of the line unbounded to drive_cmd(..., buf, 128). A 116-char name and a 110-char command string test both limits. Empty names must fail cleanly, not match the first registry entry.

name: bad_args_disk
why: Every disk sub-option given missing, garbage, negative or hex arguments must print its usage or failure line. parse_name_rest truncates names at 31 chars, so a 100-char name followed by YES must not turn into a valid name, and its tail must not be read as the YES token. YES is only ever sent with nonexistent disk names, so nothing gets erased. (Fixed: bare 'disk -read' / 'disk -write' / 'disk -use' hit shell.c's own Usage branches.)

name: bad_args_mon_and_dol
why: mon has no undashed aliases (it uses strcmp), so 'mon list' / 'mon -list extra' must be rejected. Number parsing must reject empty, negative and decimal input. PID 0 must be refused for both kill and create. (dol steps covered by dolphin_help_and_shell_side_errors were dropped.)

name: huge_numeric_args
why: parse_number rejects values that overflow uint32 instead of wrapping, so 4294967296 must not become PID or LBA 0. 4294967295 is accepted, but the shell and scheduler print PIDs with int_to_str((int)pid), so it probably shows as -1 and 2147483648 as a negative number. That is a display defect to flag, not a crash. 'mon -debug 5 junk' is accepted because parse_number stops at a space, so trailing junk is silently ignored. Reading or writing LBA 0xFFFFFFFF must fail the capacity check.

name: spawn_kill_slot_reclaim_34x
why: 34 create/kill cycles is more than TASK_POOL_CAP=32 and the 32 static stacks. If kill fails to return the pool slot, the stack (task_free_stack) or the private PML4 (vmm_free_pml4), a later spawn fails with 'Task pool exhausted', 'Failed to allocate task stack' or a vmm_alloc_pml4 error. Only one debug task is alive at a time, so the multi-task scheduling problem does not affect this case. Auto-PID 'mon -debug' must refuse while a task exists and work again after ultramon.

name: two_debug_tasks_shell_starvation
why: Regression (fixed round 1: STARVE_PICKS anti-starvation in scheduler.c pick_next). The shell runs on the PRIORITY_IDLE TCB. pick_next() only falls back to lower-priority queues when no other task shares the current priority, and debug_task_function yields every 10 iterations. With TWO Normal debug tasks they yield to each other forever and the shell never runs again. This used to hang the prompt after the second spawn on both GRUB and UEFI. The shell must stay responsive.

name: pool_limit_32_and_beyond
why: TASK_POOL_CAP=32 includes idle, so 31 debug tasks fit. The 32nd and 33rd must fail with 'Task pool exhausted' or 'no free task slot', without corrupting g_task_pool or overrunning g_task_stacks. Killing one task must free exactly one slot. Each task also allocates a private PML4, so the vmm may run out first; that must also fail cleanly. If phase2 selftest tasks still hold slots the limit is lower, so the expectations only require a clean failure, never a fault. It used to hang at step 3 through the two-task starvation defect (now fixed; see two_debug_tasks_shell_starvation).

steps.expect: Task pool exhausted|no free task slot|Failed to create debug task
Task pool exhausted|no free task slot|Failed to create debug task
Task pool exhausted|no free task slot|Failed to create debug task

name: one_task_running_while_shell_used_grub
why: GRUB path: PIT IRQ0 at 100 Hz preempts the shell every 10 ticks to run task 700, which yields back every 10 loop iterations. Every shell command, including heavy console output and FAT/Rust calls, must still work when preempted mid-command; this tests re-entrancy of the console and the Rust allocator. The second 'mon -list' runs ~20 s later (delay_before); compare the recorded Runtime values in report.json: it should be non-zero and growing.

name: one_task_running_while_shell_used_uefi
why: UEFI path: there are no IRQs, but timer_poll() in the kmain loop calls scheduler_tick, so the shell is still switched to task 700 from the poll path. While 700 runs nothing calls timer_poll, so ticks undercount. The second 'mon -list' runs ~20 s later (delay_before); task 700's recorded Runtime may stay small or 0, which is expected from the poll design, but the shell must stay responsive.

name: uptime_rtc_accuracy_20s_idle
why: Idle ~20 s (delay_before on step 4) between two uptime/cl/timer samples; report.json records ticks, RTC time, uptime_ms and host_time per step. Checks to read off the records: (a) delta ticks / 100 vs host delta: GRUB (IRQ0 PIT) within +/-0.5 s; UEFI poll mode may undercount (known design limit) but must never overcount. (b) Seconds == ticks/100. (c) Uptime (ms) == ticks*10. (d) RTC delta within +/-1 s of host delta. Never a fault.

name: uptime_accuracy_under_output_load
why: 32 output-heavy commands between two uptime/RTC samples (recorded with host_time in report.json). Compare delta ticks / 100 with the host and RTC deltas. On UEFI, console redraw between timer_poll() calls can take longer than one PIT period, so uptime is expected to fall behind; more than 10% drift is a finding. On GRUB, IRQ0 must keep it within +/-0.5 s.

name: uptime_accuracy_with_task_running
why: One CPU-bound task runs while ~20 s pass (delay_before on step 5); samples are recorded in report.json. GRUB tick count must still track wall time because IRQ0 fires regardless. On UEFI the task never calls timer_poll, so time stops advancing while it runs; expect a visible undercount against the RTC and report it. The shell must stay responsive.

name: fs_setup_scratch_usb0
why: All later UEFI FS cases run on usb0, the 64 MiB xHCI scratch stick (UNSAFE-qemu-usb-data.img). The UEFI boot stick shows up as usb1 and is protected (LOCKED); it must never be wiped. (Originally written for usb1: in this QEMU disk set the scratch stick is usb0 and usb1 is the boot stick.) After a fresh format the volume uses 512-byte clusters (spc=1 for 131072 sectors), so one directory cluster holds 16 entries. The directory-growth case relies on that.

name: fs_path_and_8_3_edge_cases
why: to_sfn rejects, and never truncates, names with a base over 8, an extension over 3 or a total over 12; multiple dots; a leading dot; '.' or '..'; and any char outside [A-Z0-9_-~]. The shell itself silently truncates filenames at 20 chars, so a 26-char name gives 'Invalid command format' on write and a truncated, still invalid, lookup on read. chdir treats 'root' and '..' specially: 'go root' goes to / even when a ROOT dir exists, and a dir named BACK can be entered while 'go back' is refused. 'back' at / prints 'Already at root directory'; 'go ..' at / succeeds as a no-op. Regression (fixed in find_dir_cluster): from a first-level subdir, 'cp WELCOME.TXT ..' resolves the '..' entry, whose cluster is 0 (meaning root); that 0 used to reach write_file_at and fail valid_cluster, so 'Failed to copy file' appeared and the later read/rm of WELCOME.TXT at / failed too. 'cp X <99-char dir>' passes a 99-byte destination to name_arg (MAX_NAME 64) and must fail cleanly.

steps.expect: Changed to parent directory|Already at root

name: write_content_truncation_and_overwrite
why: The shell copies at most 100 content bytes (content[101], j<100), and a typed line holds at most 127 chars. So 115- and 188-char contents must be stored as exactly 100 chars (the 188-char one is cut to 127 by the line editor first). Truncating silently with no warning is a usability defect worth flagging; a 101st char would be a buffer overrun. Overwriting a file must replace its content and free the old cluster chain. Whitespace-only content and every printable punctuation char must round-trip, since the shell does no metachar handling.

steps.send: write S.TXT a b  c   d

steps.expect: File content: a b  c   d

name: repeated_create_delete_cycles
why: 12 write/read/rm cycles on one name, plus 3 cycles of mkdir/enter/write/rm/back/rmdir, must reuse 0xE5 directory slots and free clusters every time. There must be no 'already exists', no stale content from an earlier cycle (each read must show the matching v<i>), and nothing left behind in ls or listsys.

name: directory_growth_and_dirent_reuse
why: Filling the 64 MiB volume with 100-byte 'write' commands would take about 127k commands, so a truly full disk cannot be reached from the shell. Instead this case fills a directory. 36 entries plus '.' and '..' span 3 directory clusters, which exercises the chain extension in find_free_dirent (alloc + zero + link) and for_each_entry across cluster boundaries. After deleting everything, re-creating 18 files must reuse the 0xE5 slots without bringing back old F*.TXT names; a zeroing bug in the extension cluster would show up as ghost entries. The emptied GROW directory, now 3 clusters long, must be deletable.

name: deep_nesting_19_levels_search_and_listsys
why: 19 nested 8-char directories make cwd_path about 166 chars. CWD_BUF is MAX_PATH=128, so the prompt path must be truncated, not overflowed. Regression (fixed round 1: search_rec/list_rec now prune past MAX_DEPTH): AAA is created before ZZZ, so 'search TARGET.TXT' used to hit the depth error inside AAA first and reports 'File not found' even though /ZZZ/TARGET.TXT exists, and listsys stops early without printing /ZZZ/. 'back' x19 must land exactly at /, since the path string is shortened with rfind('/'). The case removes the whole tree level by level afterwards.

name: raw_disk_bounds_and_locks
why: usb0 (64 MiB scratch stick) has 131072 sectors, so LBA 131071 reads and 131072 must fail, and out-of-range writes must be refused. Writes only touch sectors near the end of usb0, outside the FAT area these tests use, and are zeroed again afterwards. Hex parsing ignores spaces, pads an odd nibble count with '0' (ABC -> ABC0), and stores non-hex input as text. 'disk -write 130000' with no payload writes a zero sector. nvme0 is internal and MASTER-LOCKED: write, wipe YES and install YES must all be refused. 'disk -master nvme0' without YES only prints the warning; YES is never sent. Arming a wipe on vda and then confirming one on usb0 must be rejected ('another disk is armed'). vda is the virtio scratch disk and is wiped to clear the arm. Reselecting usb0 must remount its FAT volume intact.

name: disk_install_usb0_scratch
why: The full 'disk -install usb0 YES' path on the scratch stick. It stages BOOTX64.EFI and KERNEL from another USB or virtio volume, never from NVMe, then formats and writes the layout. Under UEFI the boot stick (usb1) holds the files, so install should complete; under GRUB (CD-ROM boot) no disk holds them and install fails cleanly. Expect accepts both outcomes; the step must not fault, and usb0 must stay selected and mounted afterwards. Run near the end, since it replaces usb0's contents.

The harness waits for one prompt per Enter. The case also sends a burst of bare Enters, a full 127-char line immediately followed by another command, and interleaved backspaces.

name: regression_round1_mem_units_and_dotdot
why: Regressions for kernel bugs fixed in shell-test round 1. (1) meminfo.rs format_bytes truncated to whole GB, so ~4040 MiB printed as 'Total Available: 3 GB' (and drive -info mem 'avail=3 GB'); it now uses MiB below 16 GiB like memory.c. name: ported_disk_switch_fat_isolation
why: Ported from shell_tests.py (fs-disk-switch-isolation, bug #13). Switching the selected disk must not flush one volume's FAT/dir cache onto another. Uses the two scratch FAT volumes vda (virtio) and usb0 (xHCI) instead of master-unlocking nvme0, so internal disks stay locked. name: ported_reboot_repeat_persistence
why: Ported from shell_tests.py (boot-repeat, fs-persist-across-reboot). Four HMP system_resets in a row: each boot must reach the shell (catches intermittent loader/early-boot hangs, e.g. the open UEFI loader stall), the uptime must restart (< 100 s), and the files and the VD directory written to vda by ported_disk_switch_fat_isolation must still be there. persistence_across_reboot covers a single reboot on usb0.

name: regression_boot_disk_identity_and_install_source

Before, a Popcorn-formatted scratch stick holding the test-only loader was guessed as the boot disk and its loader was installed.

name: stop_halts_cleanly
why: Run this LAST: stop prints the warning, then writes the QEMU (0x604/0xB004) and VirtualBox poweroff ports. QEMU should exit; if it doesn't, the kernel prints 'Halted. It is safe to power off.' and hlt-loops. QEMU exiting or no further prompt both pass (allow_exit) as long as the shutdown text appeared and no fault did. (Merged with the former stop_shutdown case.)
